title: food-insecurity-nigeria: small-area estimation of severe household food insecurity across Nigeria's 774 LGAs
description:
Code and derived area-level results for a Bayesian small-area analysis of severe household food insecurity across Nigeria's 774 Local Government Areas, from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, fitted in R-INLA.

The release carries the manuscript, the four propositions with proofs and their numerical checks, the identification bounds for the 120 areas holding no sampled cluster, and four spatial cross-validation designs with pass rules fixed before fitting. Headline results: 115 of 774 areas above a 50% prevalence threshold with a 95% interval of 101 to 130; a feasible standard deviation for that count anywhere from 0.156 to 74.11 given the marginals alone; an identified count of 87 to 231, of which 120 of the 144-wide interval is assumption; and coverage of 0.890 at the exposure the unsampled areas actually face, against a nominal 0.95.

Not included, by licence: the DHS microdata, which cannot be redistributed and is available to registered users from the DHS Program. Household-level derived tables are excluded for the same reason. The walkthrough video is excluded from the archive because its soundtrack is a commercial recording.

Code is MIT; results and documentation are CC BY 4.0.
notes: Submitted to the Journal of Mathematical Sciences, National Mathematical Centre Abuja, Vol. 8 Issue 1. Add an ORCID iD to the creator record before publishing the DOI.
